problem_type: history pagination error state reset by callback identity churn
symptom: After a history-page read fails, a same-session parent rerender with a newly allocated onLoadOlder callback hides the visible history error before the user retries.
direct_cause: AgentPanelV4Panel reset historyError in a layout effect keyed by onLoadOlder, although the resident shell supplies that callback inline on every parent render.
class_root: The panel treated callback identity as session identity instead of using historyIdentity for session resets and the explicit retry boundary for error dismissal.
affected_population: Users viewing a V4 Agent panel whose host rerenders while history pagination has failed
Resident and devlab hosts that pass an inline or otherwise unstable onLoadOlder callback
internal_only_reason: The invariant is local application lifecycle behavior; no external specification decides when a user-visible pagination error may be cleared.
invariants: historyError remains true across same-historyIdentity rerenders until a new retry begins or the history identity changes.
Only the history identity reset and the explicit pagination retry clear a prior history error.

door_reduction.why_not: The state is owned and rendered inside one panel symbol; all host callbacks converge on that single state owner, so there is no second read/write door to merge.

generality_proof: Every host supplies historyIdentity and onLoadOlder to the same AgentPanelV4Panel state owner. Removing callback-identity resets preserves the error for every equivalent host while the existing identity reset and retry path continue to clear it at their shared boundaries.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The panel owns pagination lifecycle state and the test evaluates the actual frozen hook body with the installed React renderer.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own historyError lifecycle and clear it only on history identity changes or explicit retry.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The host allocates the callback during parent renders; the panel now ignores that identity churn for error lifecycle.
The fixture consumes the same panel implementation and therefore the same historyError owner.

recurrence.reason: Any parent rerender that creates a new callback identity can reproduce the lost error while the session remains unchanged.
same_class_scan: Ran rg for setHistoryError and onLoadOlder across src/workbench/ai/v4 and its hosts; all historyError writes converge in AgentPanelV4Panel.
Ran node scripts/door-map.mjs historyError; it found the single rendered state door in AgentPanelV4Panel.
Checked ProjectAgentResidentShell and devlab V4 panel consumers for unstable callback allocation.

prevention.invariant: Callback identity changes cannot clear historyError; only session identity changes and a new retry do so.
prevention.failure_mode: A stale error remains visible until the user retries or the panel changes history identity, preserving the failure signal.
prevention.strategy: Keep lifecycle reset keyed to the semantic history identity and keep retry dismissal at the scroll admission boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: The callback-identity reset was the obsolete behavior that caused the regression and is deleted in the same change.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The defect is caused by local React hook dependencies, not by a third-party dependency lifecycle.

migration: No persisted state or external contract changes; existing mounted panels use the semantic identity and retry boundaries on their next render.
residual_risks: The full Electron host journey is not exercised by this unit test; host callback wiring is covered by the repository source scan and the shared panel hook test.
